1 Introduction

1.1 This Code of Practice concerns the principal methods used by police to identify people in
connection with the investigation of offences and the keeping of accurate and reliable
criminal records. The powers and procedures in this code must be used fairly, responsibly,
with respect for the people to whom they apply and without unlawful discrimination. Under
the Equality Act 2010, section 149 (Public sector Equality Duty), police forces must, in
carrying out their functions, have due regard to the need to eliminate unlawful
discrimination, harassment, victimisation and any other conduct which is prohibited by that
Act, to advance equality of opportunity between people who share a relevant protected
characteristic and people who do not share it, and to foster good relations between those
persons. The Equality Act also makes it unlawful for police officers to discriminate against,
harass or victimise any person on the grounds of the ‘protected characteristics’ of age,
disability, gender reassignment, race, religion or belief, sex and sexual orientation, marriage
and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity when using their powers. See Note 1A.
